chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār wrote to Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام:

Regarding a woman whose husband has died while she is in her waiting period, and she is in need and finds no one to provide for her, and she works for people: is it permissible for her to go out, work, and stay away from her home at night for work and need during her waiting period?
He said: so he عليه السلام wrote in reply, 'There is no harm in that, if Allah wills.'

key_terms.تَخْرُجَ: to go out from her residence
key_terms.عِدَّةٍ: the waiting period a woman observes after the death of her husband
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible
key_terms.مُحْتَاجَةٌ: being in financial need or hardship
key_terms.يُنْفِقُ: to provide maintenance or financial support

ai.seo_question: Can a widow in her ʿiddah leave home and work if she has no one to support her?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a widow in her ʿiddah who has financial need and no provider. It permits her to leave home, work, and even stay away overnight when required by work and necessity, showing accommodation in the law for hardship and livelihood.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4784 - Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar wrote to Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ali (as)

regarding a woman whose husband had passed away while she was still in her waiting period (iddah) and who was in need, with no one to provide for her, and she worked for people.
He asked whether it was permissible for her to leave her house, work, and even stay away from her home overnight for work and necessity during her waiting period.
Imam (as) responded: "There is no harm in that, God willing."
